transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

This is a very common issue with built-in dishwashers. When the door 'crashes' down instead of staying open at an angle, it almost always means the mechanical balance system has failed. The most likely cause is that one or both of the small metal springs inside the hinge mechanism have snapped or come detached over time. Before we look for parts, please check the hinges carefully: open the door fully and inspect the top and bottom of each side hinge. Do you see any broken springs or loose cables? This will tell us if it's a simple spring replacement or something more involved.

I had a look under the plinth with a torch and can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side. The left side still has a bit of tension but the right has none. I heard a twang last week when it went.

To get the correct replacement parts, I need your model number. It’s usually on a sticker on the side edge of the door frame—can you read it for me?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The sticker on the door edge is partly peeled, but I can see it starts with LTF. I can't read the rest of it, sorry.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
That suggests it: the right-hand balance spring has detached or snapped. This is a standard mechanical wear item on Hotpoint dishwashers and is safe to replace yourself. You don't need the model number to find the part; most Hotpoint built-in dishwashers use the same pair of springs (one for each side). You can buy a 'dishwasher door hinge spring kit' from any major DIY store or online retailer—they are very inexpensive. To fit them: unplug the dishwasher, open the door fully to access the hinges under the plinth, and remove the broken spring. Note how it hooks onto the arm and the frame, then attach the new one with similar tension on both sides. If you find the hinge arms themselves are bent or loose, you may need a full hinge assembly, but usually just replacing the springs fixes the 'crashing' door.
Ok thanks. I can't pull the machine out though, it's screwed to the worktop and the plinth is tight. Is there a way to fit the spring without sliding it out?

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
Yes, you can usually replace the spring without pulling the dishwasher out. Because it is built-in and screwed down, your best route is to work through the gap under the plinth or by removing just the bottom door panel if that is accessible. 1. Unplug the machine for safety.
2. 3. Use a long pair of needle-nose pliers (or a small screwdriver) to hook into the end of the loose spring on the right side. You need to pull it taut and hook it back onto its anchor point on the frame or arm.
If the spring has snapped and you only have one half, you will need to buy a replacement 'dishwasher door balance spring' (often sold in pairs). These are very cheap and standard sizes usually fit Hotpoint models.
5. Once the right side is re-attached, check that both sides move smoothly together when you open and close the door gently. If you cannot reach the anchor point with pliers through the gap, your next option is to unscrew the bottom front panel of the dishwasher door (the part visible from outside) to get better access to the hinge arms. Let me know if you need help identifying which screws to remove for that panel.
I'm not sure I can reach it through the plinth gap with pliers, it's pretty tight. I don't think I can get to the bottom door panel screws either, the decor panel is in the way. Is there another way?

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
Given how tight the space is and that you can't reach the anchor point with pliers, trying to force it yourself risks damaging the hinge arms or the cabinet. The most practical solution here is to call in a qualified engineer who has the tools and experience to safely remove the door panel or manoeuvre the unit just enough to re-hook the spring.
